thread:
maya: Ran the synthetic workload dry-run this morning against prod-mirror for the Black Friday mix. Wanted to share quick findings and flag mitigation options.
raj: Nice — did you run both chat and embed-heavy mixes?
maya: Yep — 60% chat (long tail tokens), 30% embeddings, 10% rerank. 6h window at step-up QPS sim to model a 3x sustained surge + microbursts (30s spikes ~6x).
jordan: TL;DR numbers?
maya: Baseline we see ~8k GPU-hours/day. For the 6h surge window projected additional demand ~14k GPU-hours (so ~22k GPU-hours for the day). Microbursts push momentary concurrent GPU demand ~= 2.8x baseline.
serena: That projection seems higher than our naive linear scaling estimate. What bottlenecks caused the extra GPU-hours?
maya: Two things: 1) chat long-context increases KV cache pressure -> memory fragmentation causing some tasks to requeue, reducing packing efficiency; 2) tail latency SLOs triggered more retries during microbursts, which amplified token work.
sam-oncall: Any region hotspots?
maya: us-west1 and eu-west3 saw most of the pressure. us-east1 had capacity headroom thanks to recent prewarm.
raj: What about autoscaler behavior? Did cluster-autoscaler keep up?
maya: Autoscaler did add nodes but with ~45–60s delay. That delay matters when spike is 30s bursts. We lost packing efficiency and hit queuing.
jordan: We should consider a prewarmed burst pool + faster scale-up policy for BF window. Cost tradeoff?
serena: Estimate the cost: 14k extra GPU-hours * $0.75/hr reserved = ~$10.5k. If we use reserved prewarm instead of on-demand, add base monthly commit delta ~ $5k pro-rated. But avoids SLO penalties and retries.
maya: Alternative: route microburst traffic to quantized 4-bit model variants for low-priority routes (rerank/embeds) and keep full precision for core chat. That would cut per-token GPU time ~30–40% during peaks.
raj: Do we have a safe routing policy to fall back to quantized variants? Need to ensure quality checks for chat.
maya: Yes, we tested gated fallback for rerank+embeds. For chat we can do a percentage-based canary: 20% shard to 4-bit variant during surges and monitor regression metrics.
sam-oncall: What about cache warm-up? How long to refill KV cache for gen models?
maya: On a cold start for a model family it takes ~15–25 minutes to warm top-10 prefixes across our traffic mix. For microbursts that's unacceptable. Suggest maintaining a small sticky KV cache in prewarm nodes and run lightweight synthetic prefix traffic to keep hot entries alive.
jordan: Can we run a lightweight background job to maintain cache? Low-cost — maybe 1–2 GPUs per region.
maya: Yes. I ran a sketch of the job:
```
# simulate short prefix churn to warm KV
./prefix_warm --region us-west1 --model redwood-7b --qps 20 --duration 24h
```
deploy-bot: scheduled job prefix_warm_us-west1 starting 2027-11-20T04:00:00Z :white_check_mark:
serena: Any networking issues surfaced? Packet drops, load-balancer saturation?
maya: ALB stalled ~2% of requests at peak due to connection reuse limits on some edge nodes. Increasing keepalive pools and moving to HTTP/2 multiplexing cut retries by half.
raj: So concrete mitigation list?
maya: Proposed runbook for BF window: 1) Prewarm 4 GPUs per hot region (us-west1, eu-west3) starting 24h prior. 2) Enable short-lived reserved burst pool (50% oversubscribe budget) with autoscaler fast-path (targetCPU -> 30s). 3) Route non-critical traffic to quantized variants automatically during >2x baseline. 4) Launch prefix_warm jobs to maintain KV. 5) Increase ALB keepalive and switch edge -> HTTP/2 where possible. 6) Monitor token-retry and tail-latency dashboards with paging thresholds.
sam-oncall: Oncall actionables: I'll add the alert runbook for token retry rate >0.8% and queue-length >2000 and wire paging to SRE.
jordan: Who owns reserved burst pool commit? Product or Infra?
serena: Infra will own the orchestration, but finance needs a short approval for the pro-rated reserve cost. I'll loop in finance.
raj: Can you attach the simulation output logs? need peak QPS histogram and per-region GPU concurrency.
maya: Pasted the summary below (short):
- global peak QPS during sim: 11.9k
- 95th tail token latency baseline -> 210ms; during spikes -> 940ms
- retry rate baseline 0.12% -> spike 1.1%
- peak concurrent GPUs: 114 (baseline 41)
- projected extra GPU-hours for day: 14,200

maya: I also uploaded the full CSV to the run artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood.internal/sim/bf-dryrun-1803659120.csv
serena: Ok looks reasonable. Let's get a quick decision: prewarm + reserved burst pool + routing to quantized variants. Finance signoff needed for reserve delta.
raj: 👍 agree. maya, can you open a short RFC with numbers and call out rollback plan?
maya: Will do in #eng-prod-rfcs. Expect draft in 60m.
sam-oncall: I'll schedule the prefix_warm cron and add the new alerts.
deploy-bot: cron created: prefix_warm_eu-west3 -> daily at 04:00 UTC
maya: thanks all. Will follow up with RFC and the CSV. If anyone wants deeper numbers ping me and I'll share the raw sim instance. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
